mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises above 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over two months indicates a restrictive monetary policy with falling inflation, which typically supports risk assets by reducing uncertainty, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) above 63% for six consecutive months signals a broader labor supply, which can temper wage growth and support corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS rising for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS rises for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
